subject: EU contract - per-token definitions, streaming rounding & commit language
messages:

Subject: Clarify billable tokens and streaming rounding for EU contract

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal/procurement at Surgica are reviewing the pricing appendix and we have a few open items before we can proceed with our procurement review:

1) Billable tokens definition: your appendix references "billable tokens (per request)". Can you confirm whether that is input tokens + generated tokens, and whether we should expect any additional rounding logic applied at the request or monthly aggregation level?

2) Streaming sessions: for long-running streams (real-time transcription -> streaming tokens), how do you count partial tokens emitted over multiple frames? We need to understand if there is any rounding up per-frame that could materially increase our monthly usage estimates.

3) Commit tiers & discounts: our FP&A wants to model both per-token usage and the committed-tier discounts. Is the discount applied at invoice level or per-request pricing? Any worked example would help.

Attached is a small internal note we used for modeling. Can you respond with proposed contract language for the billable metric and a worked example for a 3M token/month commit?

Thanks,

Marta Lopez
Head of Procurement
Surgica Health

Subject: Re: Clarify billable tokens and streaming rounding for EU contract

Hi Marta — appreciate the clear list. Quick answers up front and attached a pricing matrix + worked examples.

Summary answers:
- Billable tokens = input tokens + model output tokens. We do not apply any per-frame markup beyond tokenization rounding (see below).
- Rounding: we round token counts per request to the nearest whole token (i.e., partial token fractions are rounded up). There is no extra per-frame surcharge for streaming; streaming is counted as the aggregate of request-level token counts for the session.
- Discounts: commits are applied at invoice level. Tier discount is applied to token unit price for all billable tokens in the invoice period once the commit threshold is reached. If committed tokens aren’t used, the unused portion is invoiced per the contract (or credits applied depending on the agreed refund/true-up clause).

Worked example included in the attached "redwood-pricing-matrix-v2.xlsx" (tab: EU_3M_commit). Short example:
- Baseline unit price: €0.0009/token
- Commit: 3,000,000 tokens/month -> 15% discount -> invoiced unit price €0.000765/token once threshold met
- Streaming session example: 1 session produces 2,345.4 tokens (input+output aggregated across frames) -> round up to 2,346 billable tokens for that request. Monthly sum is simple aggregation of request-level billable tokens.

Proposed contract clause (draft):
"Billable Tokens" means the total count of input tokens and generated tokens for each API request, using Redwood's tokenization algorithm. Token fractions will be rounded up to the nearest whole token on a per-request basis. For streaming requests, each streamed message is billed based on the aggregated token count for that request frame; month-end billing is the sum of all per-request billable tokens.

If you prefer, Rishi can provide a short technical appendix that defines tokenization and how partial tokens occur in streaming.

Thanks — I’ve attached the matrix and an invoice-level example. Happy to hop on a call if useful.

Best,

Subject: Re: Clarify billable tokens and streaming rounding for EU contract

Hi Julien / Marta — jumping in from product/serving side with concrete numbers so legal can see the delta. Short version: monthly-aggregation rounding slightly reduces billable counts compared to per-request rounding for many high-frequency small-frame streams, but the difference is usually small (<1% in our tests). Details below and a suggested compromise clause.

Technical example (simplified):
- Scenario A (per-request rounding): 10,000 streaming frames in a month, average raw token count per frame = 0.6 tokens (due to fractional tokens across byte boundaries). Rounding up per-frame -> 10,000 * 1 = 10,000 billable tokens.
- Scenario B (monthly aggregation): aggregate raw tokens across frames = 6,000 raw tokens -> round once -> 6,000 billable tokens.
- Delta = 4,000 tokens (66% difference in this artificial micro-example). In realistic streaming where frames have larger token counts, the percent delta shrinks substantially. Our production simulation for a real-time transcription workload shows median delta ~0.35%, 95th percentile delta ~0.9%.

Suggested contract language (aligned to compromise):
"Billing measurement: Billable Tokens will be computed as input tokens plus generated tokens using Redwood's tokenization algorithm. For streaming APIs, parties agree to monthly aggregation for the purpose of rounding: raw token counts from streaming frames will be summed per customer per invoice period and rounded to the nearest whole token at invoice aggregation. In the event that per-invoice rounding results in an uplift greater than 0.5% versus per-request rounding, Redwood will provide a usage reconciliation report and the parties will meet to review measurement methodology. Either party may request an audit (with reasonable notice) if variance exceeds 1.0%."

Why this wording:
- Monthly aggregation reduces edge-case uplifts for tiny frames (good for you).
- A 0.5% operational tolerance gives us a predictable operational boundary while offering you a lower uplift exposure than 1%.
- We keep a 1.0% audit trigger to handle pathological cases.

If you prefer 1% cap instead of 0.5%, we can escalate to commercial leadership.

Happy to provide the simulation spreadsheet (per-request vs aggregate) if helpful.

Thanks,

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick commercial response from Redwood leadership. We reviewed Rishi's simulation and the commercial impact. We can accept the monthly-aggregation rounding approach and the proposed variance handling with the following commercial concession:

1) Redwood will commit to the monthly aggregation clause as proposed by Rishi.
2) Redwood will accept a 0.5% tolerance uplift trigger (monthly) for automatic reconciliation and reporting. For variance >0.5% and <=1.0%, Redwood will provide a detailed reconciliation and credit any materially demonstrable overcharge at our discretion. For variance >1.0%, either party may request an audit.
